metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Jamaica

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results from PISA 2022 for Jamaica, based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically uses sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and standard errors that reflect the design. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name or any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the precise weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicates that the OECD accounts for sampling variability consistent with PISA’s technical standards, but the specific weight fields are not documented in this Jamaica-only factsheet.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a PISA 2022 results factsheet that summarizes proficiency levels, relative performance, and associations using OECD-published tables rather than presenting an original student-level predictive model with an explicitly described PV and missing-data pipeline. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable for extraction here because the factsheet does not report how PVs were generated/combined for an ML estimation procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text because the factsheet focuses on high-level results and points to OECD database tables and technical documentation elsewhere (Reader’s Guide and annexes), without detailing the missing-data treatment steps.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Jamaica-specific results for PISA 2022 Creative Thinking. It states that 3,873 students in 147 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 25,500 15-year-olds; the creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in 64 countries/economies including Jamaica. No additional analytic inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., specific task completion thresholds, missing-item exclusions, or subpopulation filters) are described in the provided text for the Jamaica analytic sample.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Jamaica’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Jamaica’s mean creative thinking score is 26 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33, and 52% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), compared with 78% on average across OECD countries. The factsheet also reports within-Jamaica gaps: socio-economic status is a strong predictor (explaining 3% of variation in creative thinking), girls outperform boys by 5.5 points, and students show relative strengths in evaluating/improving ideas and in written/visual expression. It further notes COVID-19-related disruptions and uses asterisk flags to indicate when sampling standards were not met, affecting interpretability of cross-country comparisons.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It does not present an original predictive modeling pipeline, algorithm comparison, or target-variable-specific ML metrics; instead, it reports OECD database estimates (means, proficiency shares, relative performance differences, and correlations) and points to specific OECD tables for technical details. As a result, fields related to ML techniques, PV combination strategy for an ML model, and structured ML findings are intentionally left empty because the provided text does not contain those methodological elements.
